clue.text: Drunk bishop in trade? That's strange!

indicators.note: something strange is odd or out of place, so these letters are put into an unusual new order

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
taken as written
taken as written
i.e., Latin id est, means 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the oddity of a bishop going into business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is read as 'that is', the abbreviation IE. 'strange' shuffles B, IN, TRADE and IE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone intoxicated by alcohol; one is simply the formal synonym.

clue.text: One man or 2

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A riddle about whether there is one man or a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' is a two-iron, a golf club, standing for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf clubs are numbered, and a 2 is short for the club called a two-iron.

clue.text: Contributory factor to natural environment

definitions.meaning: a component or ingredient of a whole
the setting where one feels at home

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a component part of something and a person's or creature's natural habitat.

clue.text: The English road builder's state before the Roman came to Rye

definitions.text: The English road builder's state before the Roman came to Rye

parts.words: The English road builder's state before the Roman came to Rye
parts.note: alludes to G. K. Chesterton's poem The Rolling English Road, whose road was made by a staggering drunkard before the Romans arrived

explanation.walkthrough: Chesterton's poem begins 'Before the Roman came to Rye ... the rolling English drunkard made the rolling English road'. Rye is a town in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton's road-maker was a reeling drunkard, so his condition was very intoxicated.

clue.text: Main craft centre in Rochester gets foreign money

parts.note: art means skill or craft

indicators.note: centre in picks the middle letter of the word Rochester

parts.note: the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries

explanation.surface: Rochester's main arts-and-crafts hub receives funds from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Rochester has nine letters, so its centre is the fifth, E. ROCHESTER is a cathedral town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road or route is an arterial one, like a major artery of the body.

clue.text: Smooth talking sometimes leads to incidents

parts.note: even means smooth or level

indicators.note: leads means the first letters of the following words, which lead them

explanation.surface: Glib talk can sometimes cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Events are happenings or occurrences, much like incidents.

clue.text: Old water-colour

definitions.meaning: Latin, the old tongue, for water

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for water is also the name of a light blue-green colour.

clue.text: Fight to curtail misgiving about rising sin

indicators.note: about means the shortened word is placed around the other piece
to curtail is to cut off the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a qualm is a misgiving or doubt

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to err is to sin or go astray

explanation.surface: A struggle to suppress doubts about mounting wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' makes sense only in a down clue, where the turned sin word reads upwards; 'curtail' drops the misgiving's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is an angry argument or row, a verbal fight.

clue.text: A new low scale set out for payments

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so these letters are laid out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A revised low pay scale is published for wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowances are sums of money paid regularly to someone, such as pocket money or expenses.

clue.text: Published correspondence exposed Latvian king

parts.note: something exposed is open to view
a Lett is a Latvian
ER, Edward Rex, is a royal cipher for a king

explanation.surface: A newspaper prints letters that unmask a Latvian monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter addressed to someone but printed in a newspaper for the public is a published piece of correspondence.

clue.text: Greeting well spoken

indicators.note: spoken means the word for well is heard rather than spelt out

parts.note: hale means healthy, in good health

explanation.surface: A salutation delivered in a cultured accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well spoken' looks like a phrase for a refined accent; here 'well' is the healthy sense, HALE, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To call out a salute or welcome is to give a greeting.

clue.text: Evading buying drinks?

definitions.meaning: dodging or circumventing a rule or problem
getting in a round of drinks at the bar

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means circumventing something, and also, whimsically, fetching a round at the pub.

clue.text: Found in Japanese middle-class house

indicators.note: found in says the letters are tucked away within the next words

explanation.surface: A suburban home of the middle classes turns up in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of 'Japanese' and the start of 'middle-class'.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for semi-detached, a type of dwelling sharing one wall with its neighbour, typical of British suburbs.

clue.text: Where horses are seen to trot badly by worried owner

indicators.note: trotting badly means the letters of trot are jumbled
a worried owner is disturbed, so the letters of owner are jumbled

explanation.surface: At the track an anxious owner watches his horse trot poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: ROTT from 'trot' ('badly') and ENROW from 'owner' ('worried'). ROTTEN ROW is the bridle path in London's Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous riding track in a London park where riders exercise their mounts.

clue.text: Girl on form succeeded in sports

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
a version is a form or variant

explanation.surface: A girl in good form wins at games.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports are pastimes or amusements, which is what diversions are.

clue.text: Complete novel, relating---

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the word relating is given a new letter order

explanation.surface: A whole novel, telling its story, trails off to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes run this clue into the next one; 'novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral can mean whole or entire, lacking no part.

clue.text: …to the French, going in different directions when liberated

indicators.note: going in means the following pieces are placed inside the compass letters

parts.note: S and N are two different compass points, south and north
taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Continuing the novel: about the French, who scatter when freed.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots continue 15-across; 'liberated' is the jokey sense of pinched, not freed.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberated is humorous slang for taken without permission, i.e. pinched.

clue.text: Remove hospital worker from disorderly house

indicators.note: from means the worker is taken away out of the word disorderly

parts.note: an orderly is a hospital attendant
a lodge is a small house

explanation.surface: An order to eject a hospital employee from a brothel.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'disorderly house' looks like a brothel, but the worker is taken from the word 'disorderly', leaving DIS, then house is LODGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge is to force something out of position, to shift or eject it.

clue.text: Elite soldiers take aim first — and last!

indicators.note: first says the word for aim is placed before the other pieces

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim
U means upper-class, the elite
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Crack troops are told to aim before anything else and also at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage; 'take aim first' puts END ahead of U and RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to go on or survive over time, as does something that endures.

clue.text: Take a small amount of gas to fall asleep

parts.note: a drop is a small quantity of liquid
taken as written
F is the chemical symbol for fluorine, a gas

explanation.surface: Someone takes a whiff of anaesthetic and nods off.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is an idiom for dozing or nodding into sleep.

clue.text: Portrait in profile

definitions.meaning: a head-and-shoulders picture fading at its edges
a short descriptive sketch of a person

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a small picture with softly fading edges and a brief written character sketch.

clue.text: Clot causing chaos in kitchen

indicators.note: causing chaos means disorder, so the letters of the next word are thrown about

explanation.surface: A fool wreaks havoc in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' looks like a noun for an idiot, but it is the verb, to congeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauce that clots becomes stiffer or more solid, which is to say it gets denser.

clue.text: Tax loophole revealed in trial

parts.note: to try is to tax or strain, as in try one's patience
an out is an escape route or loophole

explanation.surface: A tax-avoidance scheme comes to light in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryout is a test or audition, a trial run.

clue.text: What every man is over forty, according to Shaw

definitions.text: What every man is over forty, according to Shaw

parts.words: What every man is over forty, according to Shaw
parts.note: refers to George Bernard Shaw's quip from Man and Superman that any man past forty is a rogue

explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's maxim calls every man past forty a villain or rogue.

clue.text: Regretting almost complete loss of fortune

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: ruing means regretting

explanation.surface: Someone laments having nearly lost all their money.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial ruin is the total collapse of one's wealth.

clue.text: Model ends up in Easy Street given training

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the picked letters are read upwards, backwards
ends picks the last letter of each of the following words

parts.note: PE is physical education, training

explanation.surface: A model leads a comfortable life once she has been trained.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'Easy Street' are Y and T; 'up' turns them to TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a model or exemplar, a typical example.

clue.text: Contrary toss-up with old coin

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: a lob is a high toss up into the air

explanation.surface: A coin flip decided against someone, using an ancient piece of money.
explanation.walkthrough: LOB and O together are turned round by 'Contrary'. An obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The obol was a minor silver piece of currency in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Drastic cure for dead bird

definitions.meaning: abrupt total withdrawal from an addictive drug
a turkey that is cold, i.e. dead or cooked and cooled

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for sudden complete withdrawal from drugs, and literally a chilled turkey carcass.

clue.text: A point, frequently silly

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A foolish remark is made at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft can mean feeble-minded or foolish, as in 'soft in the head'.

clue.text: Waiting in the crowd

definitions.meaning: the number of people present at an event

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both serving someone (being in waiting) and the number of spectators who turn up.
